title: [PoC] Wayland: Use IME events for composition

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Inspired by whatever GTK does (builtin IME thing?), I've tried using IME events to preview the current XKB composition sequence.

It does some interesting things, so I'm leaving this up as a PoC to collect feedback on this idea.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ad7aa73-4954-47d4-8a43-8bf1ce5432ba

(Sorry for the crappy example video, I should've installed a key preview thing, and I don't know many interesting compose sequences, but I hope that it sends the message across)

### Preview Characters

This is the "weirdest" part of it all, and the biggest reason I'm pushing this here as a PoC rather than finishing it.

Since not all diacritics are available "standalone", for visualization purposes I've used combining characters attached to a non-breaking space, which are apparently the correct way to this, according to [this source](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38126512/can-a-combining-character-be-used-alone-in-unicode). It also points out that the compatibility decomposition of spacing modifiers (the standalone diacritics) _is_ a nbsp (older versions apparently used a regular space) with the combining equivalent.

This required patching the Inter font though, as its space characters didn't have anchors (where combining characters are stuck on). My fork is available at the [`whitespace-anchor`](https://github.com/deralmas/inter/tree/whitespace-anchor) branch of my fork, which I've included in this PR. The other fonts we use are fine.

Do note that this whole thing is exclusively preview-related. Whatever is composed is the actual committed string.

### What's left

Mainly, making sure that this works alongside an actual IME. I didn't write the Wayland IME implementation myself and I haven't worked with the Godot IME API before, but it looks like it's way less stateful than I thought. Arguably, I think that we could either skip this "visualization" if an IME is active, or just send a `IMEUpdateEventMessage` before a `IMECommitEventMessage` every time, so that they can hopefully coexist.

I need to obviously double-check (it seemed to map sequentially to Unicode) and annotate the "dead key" table, which we need as `xkb_keysym_to_utf32` returns nothing with dead keys (obviously).

We could also consider handling visualizing "unicode keysyms", which could potentially cover even more characters, although I'm not entirely sure how they work and if they actually require extra logic.

(Again, if we mistakenly visualize a character wrong it's fine, as we'll commit whatever libxkbcommon spits out anyways)
